sessions.title: Exodus Trail
sessions.theme: Law, wilderness, and covenant moments

clues: I spent years tending sheep far from the palace where I was raised.
A desert encounter changed my assignment and my confidence.
I kept bringing the same demand to a stubborn ruler.
I led a nation through the sea and into the wilderness.
I received God's law on Mount Sinai.
rounds.teachingNote: Moses is identified by the burning bush call, the Red Sea crossing, and receiving the law at Sinai; those Exodus anchors explain why he fits every clue.

clues: This observance began on a night of urgency and closed doors.
Its first meal included instructions for travel readiness.
Its sign on the outside of each home mattered greatly.
It remembers the final plague in Egypt.
It celebrates the Lord passing over marked Israelite households.
rounds.teachingNote: Exodus 12 ties Passover to the marked Israelite houses and the final plague, which is why the clues focus on blood, urgency, and deliverance from Egypt.

clues: This appeared with the morning dew and could not be stockpiled for long.
People asked a question about it before they knew its name.
It exposed whether the camp would trust God's daily care.
It was gathered in the wilderness except on the Sabbath.
It was bread from heaven for Israel.
rounds.teachingNote: Exodus 16 describes manna appearing with the morning dew and being gathered daily, so the clues point to God's wilderness provision.

clues: I first appeared near a battlefield before I became a national leader.
Two of us gave a minority report that honored God's promise.
I was told repeatedly to be strong and courageous.
I led Israel after Moses died.
Jericho fell during my leadership.
rounds.teachingNote: Joshua is anchored by his faithful spy report, the command to be strong and courageous, and Jericho falling under his leadership.

clues: This structure moved whenever the people broke camp.
Its design came with exact instructions for fabrics, frames, and furnishings.
It placed holiness at the center of Israel's camp.
Priests served there before the temple existed.
It was the portable sanctuary in the wilderness.
rounds.teachingNote: The tabernacle was Israel's portable sanctuary; Exodus gives its pattern and then records it being set up in the wilderness.

sessions.title: Kings And Prophets
sessions.theme: Voices, rulers, and courage under pressure

clues: I spent a season receiving food in an unlikely way near a brook.
I once stayed with a widow whose supplies did not run out.
Fire became a recurring sign around my ministry.
I confronted the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel.
I was taken up to heaven in a whirlwind.
rounds.teachingNote: Elijah's clues come from the brook and widow provision, the Mount Carmel confrontation, and his being taken up in a whirlwind.

clues: My influence pushed royal power toward idol worship.
A vineyard dispute exposed how ruthlessly I used authority.
A prophet announced disaster because of my actions.
I threatened Elijah after Mount Carmel.
I was the wife of King Ahab.
rounds.teachingNote: Jezebel is identified by her opposition to the Lord's prophets, her threat against Elijah, and her role in Naboth's vineyard.

clues: I kept my practices even when empire expected assimilation.
God gave me insight into dreams and visions.
A law targeting prayer became a trap for me.
I spent a night with lions and was unharmed.
I served in Babylon with unusual faithfulness.
rounds.teachingNote: Daniel's Babylon setting, disciplined faith, dream wisdom, and deliverance from lions all point to the same exile-era servant of God.

clues: I started my mission while serving in a foreign court.
A report about broken walls moved me to tears and prayer.
Opposition mocked the work I came to do.
Builders worked with tools in one hand and weapons nearby.
I led the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls.
rounds.teachingNote: Nehemiah's clues center on his prayerful grief over Jerusalem's walls and the guarded rebuilding work that finished the wall.

clues: My rise to prominence began in a setting shaped by imperial beauty customs.
A relative challenged me to see position as responsibility.
I approached a king at great personal risk.
Two banquets played a key role in exposing a plot.
I helped save the Jews in Persia.
rounds.teachingNote: Esther risked approaching the king and used the banquet setting to expose Haman's plot against the Jews.

sessions.title: Gospel Moments
sessions.theme: People, places, and teachings around Jesus

clues: This town carried old royal associations long before the New Testament.
Travel and census pressures brought one family here at a difficult time.
Nearby fields became part of the story told to shepherds.
The Messiah's birth took place here.
This is David's town where Jesus was born.
rounds.teachingNote: Bethlehem is the city named in Micah's messianic prophecy and Luke's account of Jesus's birth.

clues: I first arrived when the streets were dark and the conversation was private.
My questions showed that I struggled to think beyond the physical.
I later urged a more careful hearing before judgment.
I am linked to the teaching about being born again.
I was a Pharisee who came to Jesus at night.
rounds.teachingNote: Nicodemus first comes to Jesus by night in John 3 and later helps care for Jesus's body in John 19.

clues: This section opens with a series of surprising blessings.
It values qualities the world often treats as weakness.
It appears near the start of a major sermon by Jesus.
It includes the poor in spirit, the meek, and the peacemakers.
These are the blessings at the start of the Sermon on the Mount.
rounds.teachingNote: The Beatitudes open the Sermon on the Mount with repeated blessings such as the poor in spirit, the meek, and the merciful.

clues: My position gave me money but not respect.
A crowd became a barrier before it became an audience.
My height influenced where I watched from.
Jesus called me down from a tree.
I was the tax collector in Jericho who welcomed Jesus gladly.
rounds.teachingNote: Luke 19 identifies Zacchaeus as the short tax collector who climbed a sycamore tree and responded to Jesus with repentance.

clues: Fishing and village life shaped many scenes in this area.
Religious elites sometimes looked down on this region.
Several disciples worked here before following Jesus.
Much of Jesus' public ministry unfolded around this area.
Nazareth, Capernaum, and a well-known lake are associated with Galilee.
rounds.teachingNote: Galilee is central to Jesus's early ministry, where He preached, called disciples, and ministered around the sea.

sessions.title: Early Church
sessions.theme: Acts-era turning points and people

clues: This gathering began with waiting rather than public strategy.
Wind and speech became unmistakable markers of what happened.
A crowd heard God's wonders in many languages.
Peter's sermon followed this moment in Jerusalem.
The Holy Spirit came on the believers at Pentecost.
rounds.teachingNote: Acts 2 places Pentecost after the ascension, when the Holy Spirit came and the gathered believers began speaking as enabled.

clues: I was known for service as well as bold speech.
My long defense retold Israel's story with sharp application.
My accusers reacted violently instead of repenting.
I saw heaven opened before I died.
I was the first Christian martyr named in Acts.
rounds.teachingNote: Stephen is identified by his Spirit-filled witness before the council and his martyrdom while praying for his killers.

clues: My work connected me to commerce and expensive fabric.
A riverside prayer gathering became the setting for a major turning point.
My household responded along with me.
I welcomed Paul and his companions into my home.
I was the seller of purple cloth in Philippi.
rounds.teachingNote: Acts 16 names Lydia as a seller of purple from Thyatira whose heart the Lord opened in Philippi.

clues: An earthquake turned my worst assumptions upside down.
I prepared for disgrace before I realized my prisoners were still present.
A late-night question changed the direction of my household.
I washed wounds before sharing a meal.
I asked Paul and Silas what I must do to be saved.
rounds.teachingNote: The Philippian jailer is tied to the midnight earthquake, his question about salvation, and his household's baptism.

clues: This journey began with harmful intent and official approval.
A sudden interruption made continuing impossible.
The traveler involved had to be led by the hand afterward.
A persecutor met the risen Jesus here.
Saul's dramatic conversion began on the road to Damascus.
rounds.teachingNote: Acts 9 records Saul meeting the risen Jesus on the road to Damascus, the turning point behind the conversion clues.

sessions.title: Poetry And Wisdom
sessions.theme: Books and voices of reflection

clues: This book often teaches by contrast rather than by narrative.
Its sayings return often to speech, work, and self-control.
A father's voice frames much of its early instruction.
It repeatedly says wisdom begins with fearing the Lord.
This Old Testament book is known for short sayings about wise living.
rounds.teachingNote: Proverbs identifies itself with wisdom, instruction, and the fear of the Lord as the beginning of knowledge.

clues: This book tests achievement, pleasure, and labor under a restless lens.
Its voice sounds observational, reflective, and sometimes unsettling.
Time, mortality, and limits are recurring concerns here.
It is famous for saying there is a time for many things.
This book wrestles with meaning and calls much of life vapor.
rounds.teachingNote: Ecclesiastes wrestles with vanity and meaning, then ends by calling people to fear God and keep His commandments.

clues: This story explores suffering without reducing it to simple formulas.
Long speeches from friends occupy much of the middle.
A righteous man loses family, wealth, and health.
God answers from the storm near the end.
This book centers on Job's suffering and perseverance.
rounds.teachingNote: Job is anchored by righteous suffering, honest wrestling, and God's final restoration after Job refuses to curse God.

clues: This collection contains both private cries and public worship.
Its contents include lament, praise, thanksgiving, and royal songs.
Many pieces were meant to be sung.
Psalm 23 and Psalm 119 both belong here.
This is Israel's main songbook in Scripture.
rounds.teachingNote: Psalms spans prayer, lament, wisdom, and praise, from the blessed man of Psalm 1 to the closing call for everything to praise the Lord.

clues: This book speaks more through imagery than through plot.
Gardens, fragrance, and admiration fill its lines.
It celebrates covenant love with poetic intensity.
It is also known by a title connected with Solomon.
This Old Testament book is a lyrical celebration of love.
rounds.teachingNote: Song of Songs is poetic love literature, using vivid imagery and covenant-like devotion to celebrate faithful love.
rounds.scriptureReference: Song of Solomon 1:1-4; Song of Solomon 8:6-7
